details.summary: This is a fantastic, highly practical recipe that hits the dietary goals for both MASLD and Type 2 diabetes perfectly, but it fails the completeness check due to a missing microwave time range in Step 2.

dimensions.feedback: The combination of lime, chili, and cilantro provides a classic, well-balanced Southwestern flavor profile. Using edamame instead of traditional black beans is a smart, firm-textured, high-protein swap that works beautifully with the acidic dressing.
Every listed ingredient is accurately accounted for in the instructions, and no surprise ingredients are introduced.

Step 2 tells the reader to microwave the vegetables but provides no time estimate. Update to include a specific range and a check, for example: 'Microwave on high for 2 to 3 minutes, checking halfway, until both vegetables are completely thawed and just warmed through.'
Lime, cilantro, and chili powder perfectly match the stated Southwestern-inspired cuisine style.
Microwaving frozen edamame and corn is the quickest, most reliable method to thaw and warm them gently without drying them out or requiring extra pots.
The computed nutrition panel accurately reflects the ingredients used, capturing the high plant protein from the edamame and the healthy fats from the olive oil.
The title matches the dish perfectly, and the intro provides warm, practical context about fiber and plant protein without relying on banned 'diet' language or liver-scare claims.
This is a vibrant, appealing, and extremely fast recipe that leans smartly on freezer staples for convenience and zero waste.

Perfectly answers both conditions. Edamame and olive oil provide lean plant protein and healthy unsaturated fats for liver health, while the corn provides a measured, high-fiber carbohydrate for stable blood sugar.

Zero added sugars; the natural sweetness legitimately comes from the sweet corn. The 21.6g of carbohydrates consists entirely of high-quality, fiber-rich whole foods, safely within the snack tier window.
Hits the Snacks & Sides brief excellently. With nearly 11g of protein and almost 6g of fiber, it functions perfectly as a satisfying, blood-sugar-stabilizing snack or a quick vegetable side.
Ingredients are ubiquitous supermarket staples, and the entire dish comes together in under 10 minutes from a cold start.

details.summary: This is an excellent, practical, and delicious recipe that perfectly aligns with the book's dietary requirements, utilizing accessible ingredients for a speedy, high-fiber, and high-protein snack.

dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is excellent. Using edamame as the bean base with classic Southwestern pairings (corn, lime, chili powder, cilantro, red onion) creates a bright, cohesive, and texturally satisfying combination.
All ingredients are listed and utilized perfectly in the instructions. No missing steps or unused items.

Instructions are thorough and appropriately detailed for a beginner. The microwave time is given as a range, includes a halfway check, provides a clear visual doneness cue ('completely thawed and just warmed through'), and includes the crucial step of draining excess water.
The recipe aligns perfectly with the 'Southwestern-inspired' label, smartly substituting edamame as a high-protein legume alongside traditional staples like corn, cilantro, and lime.
Microwaving the frozen vegetables is the ideal, time-saving method here, ensuring they are gently warmed without turning mushy.
The computed nutrition is completely plausible for these ingredients. The protein and fiber levels accurately reflect the generous amount of edamame.
The title is accurate, and the intro is inviting, practical, and devoid of any banned diet or health claims. It appropriately celebrates the utility of freezer staples.
This is a highly appealing, colorful, and vibrant snack. It feels fresh and intentional, rather than like 'diet food'.
This recipe perfectly fits the book's dual mission. It delivers whole-food fiber and plant protein for blood sugar control while keeping saturated fat extremely low to support liver health.
Zero added sugar, and it lands squarely in the middle of the snack carbohydrate window (17.4 g) using high-quality, complex carbohydrate sources (edamame and corn).
Hits every target for a snack/side: ready in minutes, perfectly portioned, and meets all macro constraints (10g protein, 5g fiber, <2g sat fat).
A true quick-prep recipe well under the 30-minute limit. Frozen edamame and corn are widely available at mainstream supermarkets, making this highly accessible.
